returns_fraud_signals::missing_evidence:.text: {"gaps":[{"id":"GAP-01","question":"What share of Alderwick's returns is actually abusive, and what does that abuse cost?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Every intervention in play is sized against the $4.2M figure, which is a trade-body benchmark (5.9% of refund value, range 1.5%-8.8%, i.e. $1.1M-$6.3M) transposed onto Alderwick's refund total. Nothing internal distinguishes an abusive return from a legitimate one. If true losses sit near the bottom of the range, a $180k/yr scoring platform with a 24-month minimum term is not payback-positive at all; if near the top, a heavier intervention is justified. The confirmed_abuse_cases field was added to the dashboard in 2026-Q2 and never populated, and there is no case management system in which a case could be opened — blank here means 'never measured', not 'zero abuse'.","how_to_obtain":"Fund the physical inspection audit of a random sample of returned units that FP&A requested in March 2026 and that was not scheduled ($60,000, one quarter, eight stores plus the returns hub). Add an associate-facing disposition field so suspected abuse can be recorded at the point of processing.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-02","question":"How much of the rise in return rate from 11.2% to 14.8% is explained by the shift in mix toward apparel rather than by any change in customer behaviour?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Apparel share of units sold rose from 31.0% to 46.0% over the same six quarters that total return rate rose, and apparel returns at 21.3% versus hardgoods at 6.2%. A mix-adjusted or within-category return-rate series would show whether behaviour changed at all. Category-level return rates before 2026-Q2 were not retained, so the series cannot be decomposed. The programme treats return rate as the headline measure of abuse; if the rise is mix, the premise for prioritising an anti-abuse intervention over a merchandising fix collapses.","how_to_obtain":"Reconstruct category-level return rates from transaction records for 2025-Q1 onward if line-item history survives, or compute a mix-standardised return rate. Ask analytics whether the underlying rows still exist even though the aggregated series was not retained.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-03","question":"What is the return rate and abuse exposure of the online channel specifically, over time, and how does the same customer's behaviour span store and online?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Online return rate is 21.0% against store 9.7% at 45% of units, and Loss Prevention's stated instinct is that online is far worse — but they say they have never been able to look. There is exactly one quarter of channel-split data and no cross-channel customer view: the returns data mart was deferred to FY28, so return history cannot be joined across channels, and Larkspur item-level detail exists only from 2026-Q1. An intervention aimed at store associates and one aimed at the online funnel are different programmes.","how_to_obtain":"Channel-split return rate time series from POS and Larkspur summary files; a scoped one-off identity-resolution exercise on loyalty-linked transactions to estimate what fraction of returners are cross-channel, without waiting for the FY28 data mart.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-04","question":"What would each candidate intervention cost to build and run, and what is the internal effort available to run it with no added loss-prevention headcount?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Only one option has any priced figure at all — Orlin at $180,000/yr plus $0.11 per scored return, which on 186,500 quarterly returns adds roughly $82k/yr in variable cost and exceeds the $50,000 CFO approval threshold. No cost has been produced for a size-chart remediation, an inspection protocol, an associate disposition field, reason-code redesign, or the manual human-review capacity that governance requires for any score-driven refusal. FY27 adds no headcount, so an option whose running cost is mostly labour may be undeliverable regardless of price.","how_to_obtain":"Ask each candidate owner (data-platform, returns-operations, merchandising, e-commerce) for a build estimate and a steady-state FTE estimate; cost the human-review queue implied by governance from expected refusal volume.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-05","question":"What would a restocking fee, a receipt requirement, or any policy tightening save, and what would it cost in lost legitimate sales and loyalty attrition?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"The restocking fee was rejected in January 2026 explicitly without a cost-benefit review, so no estimate exists of savings or of sales impact. The receipt-required trial was rolled back with no returns data collected, no comparison stores, and a concurrent remodel that reduced footfall — it is an unmeasured result, not a null one, yet a district manager cites it on the call as evidence that returns 'stopped almost overnight'. Without an elasticity estimate, the programme cannot know whether it is trading $1 of prevented abuse for more than $1 of lost sales, which is exactly the 'without degrading the experience for legitimate customers' constraint.","how_to_obtain":"Re-run the receipt or fee trial as a controlled test with matched comparison stores and pre-registered metrics, or commission a conjoint/willingness-to-return study. Note the loyalty terms constrain fees, so test the design legal would actually permit.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-06","question":"How many returns would a size-chart fix on the Tarnside line actually prevent, and what is the sales-weighted exposure?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"Tarnside shows 58% did_not_fit against 42% for apparel overall, and 14 of 40 audited SKUs deviate by more than one size increment — all Tarnside. But the audit did not weight SKUs by sales volume and made no link between affected SKUs and actual return volumes. Without that link, the size-chart route cannot be sized against the scoring platform, and it is formally out of the programme's remit (Merchandising owns size-chart governance) so an escalation would need a number to justify it.","how_to_obtain":"Join the 14 deviating SKUs to unit sales and returned units for 2026-Q2; extend the measurement audit to a volume-weighted sample of the Tarnside range.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-07","question":"How accurate are customer-selected return reason codes, and what would associates record if given a field?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"All reason-code shares carry the caveat 'customer-selected at initiation, not verified', there is no code for suspected abuse, and Returns Operations states an associate certain of fraud processes the return anyway and the system records 'changed mind'. The 34.1% did_not_fit and 12% changed_mind figures are therefore unusable as a split between merchandising causes and abuse, yet they are the only causal-looking data available.","how_to_obtain":"Compare customer-stated reason against physical inspection disposition on the audit sample in GAP-01; pilot an associate disposition field in a handful of stores and measure how often it diverges from the customer's code.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-08","question":"Is the abuse concentrated in a small number of customers, or spread thinly across many?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"A per-customer scoring platform only pays if losses concentrate in identifiable repeat returners. No per-customer view of returns exists in any system, so the distribution of returns per customer is unknown; the only signal is one store manager's recollection of a customer returning fourteen items in March. If abuse is diffuse, customer-level scoring is the wrong instrument regardless of vendor quality, and item- or transaction-level controls are the better fit — which is also what governance requires for anything shown to associates.","how_to_obtain":"Compute a returns-per-loyalty-ID distribution within the online channel alone, where Larkspur item-level data exists from 2026-Q1, as a partial proxy while the data mart is deferred.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-09","question":"Would Orlin pass a data protection assessment, could the deployment be lawful given regional data-residency rules, and how long would clearance take?","impact":"would_change_recommendation","why_it_matters":"Legal and privacy have not been engaged and no assessment has been started; assessments take six to eight weeks. Governance prohibits transferring returns and purchase data outside its region of origin or using it to train a model hosted outside that region, and prohibits displaying customer-level risk indicators to associates at the point of service — which is precisely what the product's accept/inspect/refuse recommendation does. There is no evidence on whether Orlin's hosting region or its associate-facing UI can be made compliant. If it cannot, the option is not merely weaker, it is unavailable.","how_to_obtain":"Start the data protection assessment now; ask Orlin in writing for hosting region, training-data handling, and whether the associate-facing output can be reduced to an item- or transaction-triggered inspection prompt with no customer characterisation.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-10","question":"What evidence exists that Orlin's product works in a retailer resembling Alderwick?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"The 23% fraud-reduction claim has no definition, no baseline, no named client and no described measurement; the underlying study was promised but not supplied. The 91% precision figure is scored against 'confirmed cases', which Alderwick does not have and therefore cannot reproduce. No reference customer in specialty outdoor retail was offered, and the two case studies are consumer electronics. The payback-in-five-months claim uses Alderwick's own unverified $4.2M. Absence of any independent performance evidence should cap how firmly this option is backed, whatever else is decided.","how_to_obtain":"Require the underlying study, a named reference in comparable assortment and price point, and a paid short-term pilot with a pre-agreed success metric before any 24-month commitment. Note no pilot pricing was offered, which is itself a term to negotiate.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-11","question":"What is the current returns processing cost per unit, and what is the cost of an inspection?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"An FY27 goal is to hold returns processing cost per unit flat or lower, but no baseline for that metric appears anywhere in the evidence — the field simply does not exist in the metrics set. Any inspect-on-trigger intervention raises handling time, and without a baseline and a per-inspection cost the programme cannot tell whether it is breaching its own constraint or judge the net of prevented loss against added handling.","how_to_obtain":"Returns hub and store labour costing from returns-operations; time-and-motion sample of a standard return versus an inspected return.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-12","question":"What would the affected populations — store associates and legitimate high-frequency returners — experience under each intervention?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"There is no evidence of any kind from store associates who process returns; the two store managers who responded to the all-manager request are supervisors, not the people at the counter, and 116 of 118 managers did not reply at all. Separately, the only customer research is twelve self-selected loyalty-newsletter volunteers, recruited for a checkout redesign, who were never asked about deliberate misuse and whose items were never inspected. The customers most likely to be flagged by any abuse control — frequent legitimate returners, including the two-sizes-ordering group — have no representation in the evidence. The desired outcome explicitly includes not degrading their experience and not creating associate risk.","how_to_obtain":"Structured survey or shadowing of counter associates across a stratified store sample; targeted research with high-frequency returners identified from online data, testing reaction to inspection prompts and refusal wording.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-13","question":"What refusal, appeal and record-keeping volume would each intervention generate, and does the capacity exist to service it?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"Governance requires documented human review with an override, a written reason given at the time of refusal, a stated appeal path, and 24-month retention producible on request. No one has estimated how many refusals or appeals an intervention would produce, nor who would staff the review queue under a no-added-headcount constraint. An option that is affordable in licence terms may be unworkable in review terms.","how_to_obtain":"Model refusal volume from the flag rate the vendor or rule set implies against 186,500 quarterly returns; ask legal for the minimum viable review and retention workflow and cost it in FTE.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-14","question":"How much of the returns volume is driven by supplier quality, transit damage and fulfilment error rather than customer behaviour?","impact":"would_refine_scope","why_it_matters":"Quality_or_defect, wrong_item_received and damaged_in_transit together account for 30% of 2026-Q2 returns, and revised transit packaging was approved in May 2026 on the basis of hardgoods damage claims exceeding target for three quarters. No estimate exists of the returns volume those causes represent, and both supplier quality and warehouse operations are declared out of the programme's scope. Prioritising an abuse intervention without knowing how much of the trend belongs to causes the programme has excluded risks aiming the FY27 return-rate target at something the team cannot move.","how_to_obtain":"Request defect and mis-pick rates from Merchandising and Supply Chain; measure the post-implementation effect of the May 2026 packaging change on hardgoods returns.","was_searched":true},{"id":"GAP-15","question":"Is there any organisation-wide or independent measurement of abuse prevalence outside the single Specialty Retail Council benchmark?","impact":"would_change_support_level","why_it_matters":"The $4.2M rests on one unmethodologied trade estimate whose member composition, assortment, price point, channel mix and returns policy are all unknown, and whose range spans nearly sixfold. FP&A's own addendum records that the midpoint has since been quoted in three documents without its range or its source, and the Chief Merchant now treats it as an accountable figure. No second, independent source of prevalence is connected to this brief at all. Corroboration would firm up or collapse the entire business case.","how_to_obtain":"Seek a second industry benchmark with published methodology, or peer benchmarking through a retail association; failing that, treat GAP-01's internal audit as the only admissible source and restate the plan figure as a range.","was_searched":false}]}
